requirements.title: APB Acceptance and Errors
requirements.definition: Fixed parameters N=256,Q=3329,ROOT=17, 16-bit coefficients, 8-bit addresses, and a 32-bit bus. pready is always 1; only psel&&penable constitutes an access, and a write additionally requires pwrite. Legal byte addresses are 0/4/8/12, with no alignment aliasing. An access to an illegal address asserts pslverr; while busy, any COEFF_DATA access or a CTRL write with pwdata[0]=1 also reports an error, regardless of pstrb; erroneous writes have no side effects.

requirements.title: Combinational Reads
requirements.definition: psel=1 and pwrite=0 constitute a combinational read, independent of penable; otherwise prdata=0. CTRL0 reads only mode[2:1], STATUS4 returns busy[0]/sticky_done[1]/sticky_error[2], ADDR8 returns the low 8 bits of host_addr, DATA12 returns the zero-extended 16-bit coefficient at that address when idle and 0 when busy, and reads of unknown addresses return 0.

requirements.title: Asynchronous Cancellation and Storage Retention
requirements.definition: presetn is an active-low asynchronous reset: control returns to idle, mode=1, host_addr=0, start/host_write pulses and sticky flags are cleared to 0, and irq=0; the coefficient array is not zeroed, and reset cancels the algorithm but retains committed writes. There is no obligation to check data when reading uninitialized addresses.

requirements.title: CTRL Start and Mode
requirements.definition: On a legal CTRL write with pstrb[0]=1 while currently not busy, latch mode=pwdata[2:1], and start=pwdata[0] forms a single-cycle command in the next cycle. mode1 starts the forward NTT; mode0 takes no action; mode2/3 generates an error event without modifying coefficients. mode is not updated while busy; a legal CTRL write with start equal to 0 can clear the flags.

requirements.title: Completion, Errors, and IRQ
requirements.definition: done/error events enter independent sticky states on their next sampling edge; irq=sticky_done||sticky_error, with no interrupt enable. A legal CTRL write with pstrb[0] and bit3=1 clears both flags simultaneously, with clearing taking priority over events on the same edge. Starting does not automatically clear old flags.

requirements.title: Host Address and Delayed Coefficient Writes
requirements.definition: For ADDR writes, only pstrb[0] is effective, and the address is taken from the low 8 bits of pwdata; DATA writes merge the current coefficient byte by byte according to pstrb[1:0], the higher two bytes have no effect, and there is no write if the low two bits are both 0. The legal DATA access edge latches the merged value/write pulse; the write occurs only on the next edge, to host_addr as it stands before that next edge; there is no automatic address increment. A simultaneous native core write takes priority.

requirements.title: Independent 256-Point Forward Mathematical Contract
requirements.definition: 8 in-place stages, 128 butterflies per stage, stage s=0..7; h=2^s, k=0..127, offset=k mod h, a=floor(k/h)*2h+offset, b=a+h, w=17^(offset*2^(7-s)) mod3329. First take A=mem[a] mod3329,B=mem[b] mod3329,T=B*w mod3329, then simultaneously write (a,b)=((A+T)mod3329,(A-T+3329)mod3329). Proceed in increasing s, then increasing k; no additional bit-reverse or inverse transform.

requirements.title: Forward Timing and Access Windows
requirements.definition: Let the edge accepting CTRL START be T0; busy begins at T1; the first two-cycle read phase starts at T2, followed by compute/write/advance; each butterfly takes 5 cycles, busy finally falls at T5122, and sticky_done/irq are set starting at T5123. During the algorithm, STATUS/CTRL/ADDR reads and ADDR writes are allowed; DATA reads return 0 and accesses report an error. Illegal START commands while busy are not queued.
